The bubbling dissipated when the (20x13) annulus was returned to venting via Sentry valve. - The 1HC, 2HC, 4H, 7H and the 101HC had water in the cellars, but below conductor casing. The 3H had water above the conductor casing. Slight bubbling was noted only in the 4H cellar. - All (6) wells (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to production tank and the (20x13) annuli were opened and venting to atmosphere via Sentry valves @ 12:05

Comments: On 04/04/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 Well Site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). On 03/11/2024, the violations were issued as outstanding (IR 3726997). The operator was in compliance with schedule on 03/27/2024 (IR 3736262).The following was observed during inspection on 04/04/2024:Inspection conducted after several large rain events. The beginning upper part of the channel was displaying accelerated erosion and rills entering the channel (Photos 1, 2). The opposite side of the road was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Sediment accumulation was noted within the stabilized area with establishing vegetation (Photos 3, 4). Upper culvert inlet was blocked with sediment (Photo 5).Several sections of the bank above the channel did not have temporary stabilization. A section of open soils was displaying rills leading into the channel. The channel was also displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 6, 7).The middle culvert was completely blocked with sediment. Gravel was noted above the inlet, flowing over towards the channel. Debris and channelization were noted leaving the culvert inlet (Photos 8-10).The outlet of the middle culvert had sediment accumulation within the grass and accelerated erosion below (Photos 11-15).Outlet of roadside channel was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. It was noted that sediment and flow were also both coming from the direction of the Landowner's building, in addition to the site's channel. Sediment accumulation within vegetation leading to the collection box and the site's middle culvert (Photos 16-20).Sediment accumulation within culvert and the outlet. This leads towards the stream (Photos 21, 22).Several rills leading off site and towards the roadside channel near the beginning section of the access road (Photos 23, 24). Remnants of gravel/sediment noted leading off the beginning of the access road towards the main township road (Photo 25).The violations issued on 03/11/2024 remain outstanding. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 6/08/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 6/08/2026
Violation Code: OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
Violation ID: 8277573
Permit API: 123-47192
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2026
Comments: Evidence of stressed and dead vegetation in the vicinity of the Akins lease tank battery was visible from Rounds Hill Road. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection. This inspection was conducted to document findings of an apparent release of production fluids from the Akins tank battery, as well as a separate release from a brine tank previously removed from the nearby Loomis lease's tank battery. Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners previously indicated that he had checked and found the integrity of the Loomis lease brine tank to be sufficient for future use. Kyle indicated that the tank was empty and would be unused until repurposed.The PVC drain line within the secondary containment area of the Akins tank battery was found to be improperly placed. The PVC line straddles the cutout hole in the surface of the brine tank in such a manner that fluids draining through the line would be able to flow over the surface of the brine tank and pool within the secondary containment area. Soil within secondary containment immediately below the PVC line was found to have specific conductance in excess of 17,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Evidence of pooling was visible in the containment area via crude oil staining and stressed vegetation. This indicates that fluid once filled the secondary containment, but apparently was able to migrate downward and/or outward through the secondary containment diking. Stressed and dead vegetation downslope and immediately outside the secondary containment dike further indicates the likelihood that the integrity of the secondary containment is inadequate. Understory vegetation was killed in an area approximately 30 feet wide by 200 feet long. Soils in the killzone were found to have elevated specific conductivity in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.The brine tank staged on location was found to have evidence of stressed and dead vegetation beginning from a point immediately beneath the drain valve and continuing downslope beyond the tank in an area approximately 10 feet wide by 200 feet in length. Specific conductivity in soils below the drain valve measured in excess of 8,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Soils in the killzone downslope of the brine tank were found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with brine disposal receipts for the Akins lease. The Akins Lease Akins 1 OG Well was found to have an illegible ID tag.

Comments: On August 7, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Burnett Oil Co Inc's Stickle Ross Mountain Unit 1H well (129-28648) located in Fairfield Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4011505, where the Department observed several areas of the graveled well pad to have an oily substance on it, specifically in areas relating to the reported re-plugging of the 129-28648 well. Accompanying during today's inspection is Monona Operator/Land Owner Tom Stickle and Plants and Goodwin's Representative Jim Watson.Burnett Oil representative Walter Glasgow stated in an email to the Department (documented in IR 4029448), that clean up began on 7/28/25 and was completed on 7/31/25, once the Department conducts an inspection of the site to determine if all contaminated material was removed, Burnett will replace the removed rock from the graveled well site. Once Waste Management disposes of the contaminated material, Burnett Oil will provide the Department with a quantity of the release. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed an Act 9 sign at the access road entrance to not be in compliance and inside the on-site mailbox was an outdated Emergency Response Plan (ERP). Violations associated with the Act 9 Sign and the ERP are addressed under a separate inspection for 129-28411. An access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the perimeters of the well site were observed to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative cover with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed.At the time of this inspection, the 1H: 129-28648 well appeared to be plugged and all plugging equipment appeared to be removed from the well site. A new monument and vent pipe which was reportedly approved by the Department was observed to be installed. The monument was observed to have the plugged well's permit number and replug date posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this plugged well.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the graveled well pad to be scraped in the areas that were previously observed to have an oily substance during IR 4013514. At the time of this inspection, the Department did not observe an oily or shiny brown substance anywhere on the graveled well pad. Mr. Watson stated that all contaminated material was placed in the roll off dumpster observed on site, that new gravel will be laid in the release areas and the contaminated material will be properly disposed of following this inspection. The Department requested a waste manifest for the disposed contaminated material be provided to the Department upon its receipt to verify whether the release was less than 42 gallons, and therefore remediated applicably under 78a.66(c)(1). If the quantity of the release is over 42 gallons, the Department recommends the Operator follow the Act 2 guidelines for remediation as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations issued for an oily substance on the graveled well pad shall remain outstanding at this time pending the receipt of a waste manifest and a quantity of the release.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/20/2026
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8286191
Permit API: 081-20961
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/20/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of at least 5 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and stormwater was discovered on the well pad following a re-frac on the 5H well. The notification also stated that a contractor, Tobias, would excavate the impacted pad material. I met with company man Levi Lee upon arriving on location. He showed me the location of the release. It rained steadily during this inspection. Tobias had already scraped a thin layer of gravel off of the top of the impacted area at the time of inspection. Mr. Lee said that Creston Environmental was also present to take samples and characterize the release. Some areas of the impacted pad area were more damp than others. No standing fluid was observed in this area of the well pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the pad material according to the Hanna soil conductivity meter ranged from 0.41 mS/cm to 2.86 mS/cm. The higher EC readings were found closer to the well heads and the lower readings were taken farther away from the well heads toward the southeast pad edge. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Violations noted.Violations remain outstanding for the release from June 1, 2026. These violations will be closed upon demonstration of Act 2 remediation standards.

Comments: On May 2, 2022, I conducted an inspection of the MCC West Well Site in Jefferson Township, Washington County. According to the report approximately 50-60 gallons of condensate oil was released to the well pad when a load line on a truck failed. The release was discovered on 5/1/22 at 8:10am and reported to the Department spill hot line on 5/1/22 at 9:46am. At the time of inspection, The Act 9 site ID sign was installed. The PPC plan and ER plan were on site. Three roll off disposal boxes were staged on the east corner of the well pad. The roll off boxes were labeled as Non-Hazardous Waste condensate impacted material and dated 5/1/22. The impacted area appeared to be directly adjacent to the brine tank secondary containment location. The impacted area appeared to be 40’ in length and approximately 15’ wide with a maximum depth of approximately 12 inches. No discharge was observed off the well pad and the spill did not appear to impact waters of the commonwealth. Violations are being issued for failure to control a regulated fluid resulting a release to the ground.

Comments: On 07/07/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLCs Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. An Act 9 sign and well permits are posted at the site entrance (photo #1).No standing water was observed on the pad surface.The Patterson 582 drilling rig is noted onsite; the Ron 3UH well has been drilled and the rig is currently drilling the Ron 4UH well, the Ron 5UH has yet to be drilled (photo #2). properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/03/2025 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/03/2025
Violation Code: 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
Violation ID: 8227909
Permit API: 123-47902
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/03/2025
Comments: The R H Stevenson Lease 4 conventional well is the nearest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the R H Stevenson lease. The tank battery is situated within earthen containment and consists of an upper level containing two stock tanks, and a lower level containing two polyurethane tanks. The stock tanks are plumbed into PVC piping that extends along the rear of the upper level of the earthen containment until terminating into the first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level. The first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level is also equipped with additional PVC piping apparently for the purpose of either removing or depositing fluids into the tank in the lower level of containment. At the time of this inspection, standing pools of fluid present in the upper level of the containment were found to have specific conductance measuring 5,980 microSiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). It was observed that straw had been laid down beneath the PVC piping in the upper level of containment. Where the straw cover ends, fluid was found to be actively flowing from the upper level of containment to the lower level. No fluid was observed to be flowing through the PVC piping connecting the stock tanks to the polyurethane tank during the time of this inspection. Neither polyurethane stock tank was found to have a noticeable volume of fluids contained within them at the time of this inspection. Some accumulation of fluids and crude oil could be observed around the base of the polyurethane tanks in the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection. The flow of fluids from the upper level to the lower level of containment was not found to be accumulating nor increasing the accumulated volume of fluids and crude oil present at the bottom of the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection.Approximately 40 feet south of the lower level tank battery containment area, crude oil and production fluids emerged on the soil surface. This flow of fluids continues west and is visually impacted by crude oil for approximately 180 feet. From there, soils and standing fluid with elevated specific conductance continue for approximately 75 feet before reaching a culvert. A pool of fluid at the entrance of the culvert was found to have specific conductance measuring 6,820 uS/cm.From the culvert, the fluid continues southwest in the natural swale for approximately 115 feet before reaching a point at which the swale transitions to an unnamed tributary (UNT) stream of Jackson Run, with defined bed and banks. At this point, waters in the UNT had specific conductance measuring 5,510 uS/cm. Specific conductance of 2,750 uS/cm was observed in the waters of the UNT in the remaining approximately 180 foot stretch, at which point there is a confluence with a second UNT of Jackson Run. Immediately before the confluence, waters in the impacted stream with specific conductance of 1,923 uS/cm were observed. Approximately two feet downstream of the confluence at a point with coordinates 41.95555, -79.29740 was the apparent end of impact to the UNTs of Jackson Run, where waters in the stream had a measured specific conductance of 42.6 uS/cm.At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the well.On 04/04/25 I called and spoke with William Cenk and Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. Mr. Cenk and Mr. Miller agreed to meet with Department officials onsite next week. A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Violation ID: 8203237
Permit API: 125-26999
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Hopewell Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/01/2024
Comments: On October 1, 2024, the Department conducted a routine inspection at the R Carlisle well pad in Hopewell Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination was approved for this site on October 28, 2016.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Several portions of the access road are exhibiting severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation at the time of inspection (see photo 2). The well pad appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed (see photo 3). Production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 4). The GPU units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment (see photo 5). However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of fluid leaks or discharge was observed on the ground around the GPU units. Well 7H is equipped with a well tag with no observable fluids leaking to the ground around it (see photos 7 and 8). There are four other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 6). Containment is staged adjacent to the production tanks, which appears to be for pumping operations. It is approximately half-full of rainwater at the time of inspection (see photo 9). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 10). Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that secondary containments are kept empty so they are able to mitigate the risk of a release from occurring on site as intended. The Department also recommends that GPU units and other primary containments that store regulated substances are equipped with secondary containments to mitigate the risk of discharge to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth.Violations are being issued against the severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation observed in the access road.

Comments: On February 6, 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the PF Eisaman South 43 Well Site (NOT previously approved on 6/6/2025) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 2/6/2026 (CTS 394994). Present during the inspection were operator representatives D.J Menas and Bruce Carpenter.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel. Site stabilization could not be assessed due to snow cover.At the time of inspection, there are 6 total wells on the well pad. All wells appeared equipped for production with a well tag present. No fluid leaks or spills were identified at the surface around any of the well heads or cellars. The GPUs appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Carpenter guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Carpenter the release occurred earlier in the morning on 2/6/2026 when a worker was filling a day tank in their truck with diesel from the diesel tank on the pad (photo 4). According to Mr. Carpenter, as the worker was filling the tank, they observed a leak from their tank was occurring. The worker immediately stopped pumping the diesel and pulled their truck forward. In doing so, a second smaller area of diesel release was created. According to Mr. Carpenter they are estimating 20 gallons of diesel was released on to the gravel well pad.The location of the initial release was directly adject to the onsite diesel tank (photo 5-8). The area of impacted material in this location was approximately 16 feet by 18 feet according to the operator. At the time of the inspection, the operator was actively excavating the impacted material in this area and placing it in into a roll off box.The location of where the additional diesel was released when the truck pulled forward was approximately 20 feet south of the onsite diesel tank (photo 10). The area of impacted material in this location was approximately 6 feet by 4 feet according to the operator.The Department was unable to obtain conductivity readings as the ground was frozen/heavily compacted. It was also difficult for the Department to discern any staining the release may have caused on the gravel well pad due to it actively snowing during the inspection, covering the area of the release.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation besubmitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the Eisaman 6H well for the release.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/09/2022 to BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC in Keating Twp, McKean county. SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.

Violation ID: 964821
Permit API: 083-57144
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Keating Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/09/2022
Comments: This conventional well has recently been produced with a pump jack, there was no activity on this location or throughout the Cole Creek lease during this inspection.A tank battery consisting of a 210 bbl steel stock tank and a poly brine/production water tank is located approximately 150 feet to the south of this well. These tanks are contained by an earthen dyking which has been lined and partially filled with gravel. Holes have formed throughout the exposed portion of the liner along the upper edge of the containment wall.Fluid was trickling out of the containment drain pipe into the roadside ditch upon my arrival at the tank battery. There was no supervision of this discharge and the drain is not equipped with a valve. A shower drain cover was fitted onto the inlet of this drain. The specific conductivity (SPC) of the fluid inside of the containment exceeded the upper threshold of my field meter (20,000 uS/cm). Pooled fluid in the ditch was also greater than 20,000 uS/cm. Deer tracks are abundant around the pooled fluid in the roadside ditch. This evidence suggests that the fluid being discharged from the containment drain is production water/brine. An SAC 941 sample was collected from the fluid discharging from the drain. The fluid in the roadside ditch flowed through a cross culvert and into a forested area. Poor road conditions have allowed stormwater to run off of the road surface above this culvert, which allowed the released fluid to migrate further into the forested area. Elevated SPC of pooled water and soil (along with stressed vegetation) was observed in various pathways across the forest floor west of the tank battery for approximately 200 feet downslope of the tank battery. The most downward extent of the apparent impacted soil (near a property boundary/corner marker) is approaching a channel (currently dry) that develops into an unnamed tributary of Cole Creek.After this inspection, I spoke with Justin Hansen of Bull Run to discuss the aforementioned issues along with concerns regarding the roads, site identification and actions necessary to consider this well site restored. In order to consider utilizing the containment drain, the fluid that is currently pooled inside of the containment will need to be removed along with the saturated gravel. Prior to any future discharges from the drain, the water should be tested as per the regulations to ensure it meets the criteria to be released under sufficient supervision.Future inspections will be conducted to review the current state of affairs with Bull Run personnel and evaluate remediation measures outside of the containment as they take place.
